newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-DORTMUND BEATEN AT HOME FOR FIRST TIME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-DORTMUND BEATEN AT HOME FOR FIRST TIME.

text.p: Borussia Dortmund suffered their first home defeat of the German league season on Saturday when they were beaten 3-1 by lowly Borussia Moenchengladbach after a display of indiscipline on both the pitch and the terraces.

The German champions lacked concentration in a highly-charged game which saw one player from each side sent off before halftime and an unpleasant first-half incident when frustrated Dortmund fans threw plastic cups on to the pitch and held up a corner.

Just a few days after clinching their place in the semifinals of the European Cup in which they will meet England's Manchester United, Dortmund lacked creativity and organisation against a team who are struggling near the bottom of the table.

The reigning Bundesliga champions, who also missed a second-half penalty, lost their place at the top of the table to VfB Stuttgart, who won 4-0 at Fortuna Duesseldorf on Friday. Dortmund slipped to third, one point behind Stuttgart and Bayer Leverkusen.
Swedish striker Martin Dahlin, Pole Andrzej Juskowiak and substitute Jorgen Pettersson scored for Moenchengladbach, exposing huge holes in the Dortmund defence.
Coach Ottmar Hitzfeld refused to blame his team's bad form on their intense campaign in the European Cup.
"You can't put it down to the fact that we have had a lot of games," Hitzfeld said. "We have a lot of experienced players. We have proved in the past that we can deal with that.
"We have done well to get to the semifinals. But we are going to have to lift our form in the Bundesliga to win a third consecutive title."
The home side were caught sleeping after just 20 seconds when Dahlin got on to the end of a cross from the left from wing-back Martin Schneider and headed the ball into the top right-hand corner.
When their experienced international defender Juergen Kohler was sent off in the 34th minute for his second bookable offence, Dortmund's hopes of getting out of trouble seemed to be doomed.

The crowd were angered by the decision. Five minutes before halftime Moenchengladbach midfielder Stefan Effenberg was held up from taking a corner when Dortmund fans threw plastic cups down at the corner of the pitch.
Dortmund's international libero Matthias Sammer had to plead with the fans to calm down before the game could continue. But the players were still fired up.
A minute later both teams were down to 10 men when Moenchengladbach defender Hubert Fournier was sent off for his second bookable offence.

For a while at the start of the second half Dortmund improved and they won a penalty in the 50th minute when Schneider brought down midfielder Andy Moeller in the box. But German international Stefan Reuter hit his shot straight at Moenchengladbach keeper Uwe Kamps.
In the 71st minute Juskowiak effectively sealed Moenchengladbach's shock win when he broke clear on the right-hand side of the box and slammed the ball into the back of the net.
Dortmund put on the pressure in a tense last period and scored a consolation goal in the 82nd minute when Joerg Heinrich headed in at a corner. A minute later Moeller hit the post.
But in the 89th minute Pettersson weaved his way past three Dortmund defenders to score a superb individual goal and finish off a miserable day for the champions in front of a capacity 55,000 crowd.
"We were rewarded for playing attacking football," Moenchengladbach coach Hannes Bongartz said. "We came here prepared to take risks and go forward."
Teams:

Borussia Dortmund - 1-Stefan Klos, 6-Matthias Sammer, 15- Juergen Kohler, 17-Joerg Heinrich, 14-Paul Lambert (8-Michael Zorc, 66), 16-Martin Kree, 18-Lars Ricken (Knut Reinhardt, 39), 7-Stefan Reuter, 10-Andy Moeller, 9-Stephane Chapuisat, 13-Karlheinz Riedle (11-Heiko Herrlich, 66)

Borussia Moenchengladbach - 1-Uwe Kamps, 27-Stephan Passlack, 4-Patrik Andersson, 21-Hubert Fournier, 13-Martin Schneider, 14-Peter Nielsen (3-Michael Klinkert, 46), 10- Stefan Effenberg, 7-Karlheinz Pflipsen, 8-Peter Wynhoff, 9-Andrzej Juskowiak (26-Joachim Stadler, 86), 30-Martin Dahlin (Jorgen Pettersson, 74).
